original_question: For fixed dimensions m and n and fixed norms on R^m and R^n, let z_nu = (x_nu, y_nu) be the sequence of best-approximation vectors, let M_nu = |x_nu|, and define G(Theta) = lim inf_{nu -> infinity} M_nu^(1/nu). What is the optimal lower bound for inf_Theta G(Theta), where Theta ranges over matrices satisfying the paper's nondegeneracy condition?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in Section 1, together with the setup clarified immediately around Proposition 1.2 and the partial/special-case result Theorem 1.3: the Lagarias-type problem of determining the sharp universal lower bound for the exponential growth rate of the norms M_nu of best-approximation vectors.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the relevant object G(Theta)=lim inf_{nu->infinity} M_nu^(1/nu), the fact that one studies best-approximation vectors z_nu=(x_nu,y_nu), the optimization over a class of nondegenerate real matrices Theta, and that the paper asks for a universal optimal lower bound depending only on the fixed dimensions and chosen norms.
missing_details: The matrix Theta should be specified as a real n x m matrix, not just an unspecified matrix.
The ambient integer lattice must be stated: x_nu belongs to Z^m and y_nu belongs to Z^n, so z_nu belongs to Z^(m+n).
The paper fixes two norms, one on R^m and one on R^n; the notation |x| and the error norm on the target space must be defined explicitly.
The exact definition of a best-approximation vector is missing: one must say what quantity involving Theta x - y is minimized among nonzero integer x with bounded |x|.
The ordering convention for the sequence z_nu is missing: the vectors are arranged so that M_nu=|x_nu| is strictly increasing and the approximation error is strictly decreasing.
The draft leaves the paper's nondegeneracy hypothesis implicit; this needs to be stated explicitly, not referred to vaguely.
It should be made explicit that the infimum is taken over all Theta satisfying that nondegeneracy condition, for the fixed pair (m,n) and the fixed chosen norms.
The question should define the sharp constant itself, e.g. gamma(m,n;|.|_m,|.|_n)=inf_Theta G(Theta), to make the problem stand alone.
The draft does not make clear whether the lower bound sought is exact/sharp or merely any universal bound; the paper's intent is the sharp universal lower bound.

The dependence on the fixed norms is not reflected in the notation G(Theta) alone; for a stand-alone formulation one should either include the norms in the ambient data or in the constant being optimized.
refined_question: Fix integers m,n>=1 and fix norms |.|_m on R^m and |.|_n on R^n. For a real matrix Theta in Mat_{n,m}(R) satisfying the paper's nondegeneracy assumption, let z_nu=(x_nu,y_nu) in Z^m x Z^n be the sequence of best-approximation vectors to Theta with respect to these norms, ordered so that M_nu:=|x_nu|_m is strictly increasing. Define G(Theta):=lim inf_{nu->infinity} M_nu^(1/nu). What is the sharp universal lower bound, depending only on m, n, |.|_m, and |.|_n, for G(Theta); equivalently, what is the exact value of inf{G(Theta): Theta in Mat_{n,m}(R) satisfies the paper's nondegeneracy condition}?
justification: The draft is clearly targeting the paper's opening Lagarias-type growth-rate problem for best approximations: it uses exactly the growth functional G(Theta)=lim inf M_nu^(1/nu), asks for the optimal lower bound after fixing m, n, and the norms, and ranges over matrices Theta under a nondegeneracy hypothesis. What it lacks is the fully explicit setup that makes the question stand alone: the real matrix space Mat_{n,m}(R), the lattice Z^m x Z^n, the precise best-approximation definition, the ordering of the best-approximation sequence, and the explicit quantification of the sharp infimum. Those are the details the paper supplies in the context around Conjecture 1.1 and its nearby reformulation/result in Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3.
